also.hook: Moisant built his career on the operational spine of technology organizations, infrastructure, security, enterprise platforms, and the internal systems that keep large companies running. At Indeed, overseeing 300 million monthly visitors and three million employers, he sits at the intersection of consumer scale and enterprise risk, leading both the CIO and CSO functions simultaneously.
also.name: Anthony Moisant

also.hook: Smith turned a $600K loss into an $8 million profit at Piston Group inside a single year, then spent two decades repeating that pattern of operational turnarounds across automotive and manufacturing suppliers ranging from $120 million to over $1 billion in revenue. He now sits on the board of Nikola Motor Company, the autonomous and electric truck maker, while running his own holding company, Voltava.
also.name: Bruce Smith
also.moniker: Owner, Chairman and CEO, Voltava; Nikola Motor Company board member

also.hook: C.C. Wei leads the company that manufactures most of the world's advanced AI chips. He joined TSMC in 1998 after earlier engineering roles at Texas Instruments, ST Microelectronics, and Chartered Semiconductor, and spent the next quarter century rising through business development and operating roles before becoming President and Co-CEO in 2013, sole CEO in 2018, and Chairman and CEO in 2024. Under his leadership TSMC's advanced process nodes have become the manufacturing bottleneck and enabler for the generative AI buildout, supplying the chips behind most leading GPUs and AI accelerators. He holds a PhD in electrical engineering from Yale and has repeatedly told investors that AI-driven demand for TSMC's most advanced capacity remains structurally strong even as supply stays tight.
also.name: C.C. Wei
also.moniker: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC)

also.hook: Christopher Bishop earned a BA in physics from Oxford University and a PhD in theoretical physics, on quantum field theory, from the University of Edinburgh. He began his research career in fusion plasma physics at the Culham Laboratory, then moved into applied neural computing, heading the Applied Neurocomputing Centre at AEA Technology before taking a chair in the Department of Computer Science and Applied Mathematics at Aston University, where he founded and led the Neural Computing Research Group. He joined Microsoft Research in 1997 and later directed Microsoft Research Cambridge from 2015 to 2022. In 2022 he founded Microsoft Research AI4Science, which he continues to lead. He wrote the widely used textbooks Neural Networks for Pattern Recognition (1995) and Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning (2006), and later co-authored Deep Learning: Foundations and Concepts (2024) with his son Hugh Bishop. He was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society in 2017.
also.name: Christopher Bishop
also.moniker: Microsoft Technical Fellow, founder of Microsoft Research AI4Science

also.hook: Sachdeva built a career converting large-scale corporate transactions, over $11 billion of them, into working technology systems, from integrating GE's manufacturing ERPs to modernizing Sabre's airline cloud infrastructure, before bringing that private-sector integration discipline to the U.S. Air Force as its Chief Information Officer.
also.name: Deepak Sachdeva
also.moniker: Chief Information Officer, United States Air Force

also.hook: Greg Brockman helped write OpenAI's founding announcement in December 2015 and has run its engineering effort ever since, first as chief technology officer and then, from November 2023, as president. Before that he left MIT to join Stripe in its earliest days, when the payments company was still called dev slash payments, and stayed through its rise into a major engineering organization as chief technology officer. He testified to the Senate about AI policy as early as November 2016, years before the topic reached the mainstream, and he was reinstated as OpenAI's president within days of the company's November 2023 board crisis.
also.name: Greg Brockman

also.hook: Suh spent over 23 years at IBM, rising to head global strategic partnerships worth more than $10 billion before leading Watson AI product units in commerce, supply chain and collaboration; she then served as President of DocuSign and on its board through its 2018 IPO before becoming CEO of Niantic Spatial, a company building real-world foundation models for physical AI.
also.name: Inhi Cho Suh

also.hook: Jeff Dean earned a bachelor's degree in computer science and economics from the University of Minnesota in 1990 and a PhD in computer science from the University of Washington in 1996, then worked at Digital Equipment Corporation before joining Google in 1999. At Google he co-designed MapReduce with Sanjay Ghemawat in 2004 and Bigtable in 2006, two systems that became core infrastructure for processing and storing data at massive scale. In 2011 he co-founded the Google Brain team, and in 2015 he helped design and open source TensorFlow, one of the most widely used machine learning frameworks. He also pushed Google to build custom AI accelerator chips, leading to multiple generations of Tensor Processing Units, and now serves as Chief Scientist for Google Research and Google DeepMind, helping set the company's AI research direction.
also.name: Jeff Dean
also.moniker: Chief Scientist, Google Research and Google DeepMind

also.hook: Jensen Huang founded NVIDIA in 1993 and has run it continuously ever since, first as a graphics chip maker for PC gaming and later as the dominant supplier of the GPUs that power modern AI training and inference. He holds a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from Oregon State University and a master's from Stanford, and worked at LSI Logic and Advanced Micro Devices before starting NVIDIA. Under his leadership the company introduced the GPU in 1999, a product line that eventually became the core infrastructure of the generative AI boom. He has since been recognized with engineering's biggest honors, including a share of the 2025 Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering and the 2026 IEEE Medal of Honor.
also.name: Jensen Huang

also.hook: Jim Keller has spent four decades moving between the biggest names in semiconductors, leaving a distinct architecture behind at each stop. He led design of AMD's Zen microarchitecture, the chip line credited with reviving the company's competitiveness against Intel, and earlier led the engineering behind Apple's A4 and A5 mobile processors after Apple acquired P.A. Semi. He later ran Autopilot hardware engineering at Tesla and Silicon Engineering at Intel before moving into AI accelerator chips. He is now CEO of Tenstorrent and has also co-founded Atomic Semi, a startup building small-scale chip fabs.
also.name: Jim Keller

also.hook: Krithivasan runs the largest IT services company in India and one of the largest in the world, and in September 2026 put its name on the largest AI data centre campus the country has announced: a 1 gigawatt, 250-acre, Rs 70,000 crore project in Hyderabad through the TCS subsidiary HyperVault. He reached the top of TCS after thirty-four years inside it, most of them running the banking, financial services and insurance business that is the company's biggest vertical. His stated programme as chief executive has been to build what TCS calls the world's largest AI-ready workforce, and the Hyderabad campus is the infrastructure side of that same claim.
also.name: K. Krithivasan
also.moniker: CEO and Managing Director, Tata Consultancy Services

also.hook: Lisa Su has led AMD since October 2014, combining an electrical-engineering research background with semiconductor operations experience to turn the company from a distant also-ran into a primary supplier of AI accelerator hardware. Her MI300 and MI400 series GPUs gave large AI labs and cloud providers a credible second source of high-end accelerators alongside Nvidia. Su holds three degrees in electrical engineering from MIT and built her career through technical and general-management roles at Texas Instruments, IBM, and Freescale Semiconductor before joining AMD in 2012. She was named Time's CEO of the Year in 2024 and continues to set AMD's AI infrastructure roadmap, from CES keynotes to plans for trillion-parameter-scale training clusters.
also.name: Lisa Su
also.moniker: Chair and Chief Executive Officer, AMD

also.hook: Ray Kurzweil is an American inventor, computer scientist, and author known both for his technical contributions to pattern recognition technology and for his predictions about the future of artificial intelligence. Born in Queens, New York in 1948 and trained in computer science and literature at MIT, he began founding technology companies in 1973 and in 1976 introduced the Kurzweil Reading Machine, the first device able to convert printed text into spoken words for blind and visually impaired users. He went on to develop optical character recognition software able to read text in any typeface, along with early text to speech and speech recognition systems, work recognized with the National Medal of Technology and Innovation in 1999 and induction into the National Inventors Hall of Fame in 2002. Alongside his inventing career, Kurzweil became a widely read futurist, publishing books including The Age of Spiritual Machines and The Singularity Is Near that argue technological change is accelerating toward a point where machine intelligence will exceed human intelligence. In 2012 he joined Google, where he now holds the title of principal researcher and AI visionary, leading a team working on natural language understanding.
also.name: Ray Kurzweil
also.moniker: Inventor, futurist, and Google AI researcher

also.hook: Yann LeCun helped build the technique that underlies most of today's computer vision systems. He earned a PhD in computer science from Universite Pierre et Marie Curie in Paris in 1987, working on early ideas that fed into backpropagation based neural network training. At AT&T Bell Labs starting in 1988, he developed convolutional neural networks and built LeNet, a system for reading handwritten digits that was later deployed commercially to process a large share of checks handled by US banks. He went on to become a professor at New York University's Courant Institute, founding the NYU Center for Data Science, and in 2013 joined Facebook, later Meta, as founding director and then Chief AI Scientist of its AI research division. In 2018 he shared the ACM A.M. Turing Award with Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio for their work on deep learning. He left Meta in November 2025 after roughly twelve years to launch Advanced Machine Intelligence Labs, a venture focused on building AI systems around world models rather than only predicting text.
also.name: Yann LeCun
also.moniker: Executive Chair, Advanced Machine Intelligence Labs, and former Chief AI Scientist, Meta

name: Technology Leaders
blurb: CIOs, CTOs and heads of engineering accountable for AI in production inside large organisations.

profiles.hook: Dasdan built his career on the infrastructure layer that makes large-scale data and machine learning systems actually work, from web search ranking research to leading engineering at ad-tech and networking companies, before taking the CTO role at Dropbox as the company reorients its file-storage platform around AI-driven organization and search.
profiles.name: Ali Dasdan
profiles.moniker: Data Systems Engineer Turned Dropbox CTO

primary.name: Ali Dasdan, official executive bio, Dropbox Newsroom

profiles.hook: Rabinovich arrived at the Longuet-Higgins Prize, the computer vision field's highest honor for work that has stood the test of time, the same year his startup was acquired and he became CTO of a public company. His arc from Google research to Magic Leap's human-centered AR, to founding an AI meeting tool, to leading AI at one of the world's largest freelance platforms is a compressed version of the field's own evolution: from perception research to multimodal generation to enterprise deployment.
profiles.name: Andrew Rabinovich
profiles.moniker: CTO and Head of AI at Upwork

profiles.hook: Sengupta has built enterprise AI functions from scratch at four different organizations, AXA XL, Zebra Technologies, and now JPMorgan Chase, while maintaining an active academic research career that produced over 9,100 citations and a co-authored analysis of the EU AI Act, a rare combination of frontier research credentials and boardroom-level AI deployment experience.
profiles.name: Biswa Sengupta
profiles.moniker: Chief AI Technologist and Architect of JPMorgan's LLM Suite

primary.name: JPMorgan Chase leads AI revolution in finance with launch of LLM Suite, Forbes (July 2024)

secondary.name: JPMorgan Chase, fully AI-connected megabank, CNBC (September 2025)

profiles.hook: Borrowman spent more than a decade inside Colgate-Palmolive's Hill's Pet Nutrition division building global digital marketing systems before moving to the European digital transformation role and then into enterprise AI. Her Davos 2026 appearance placed her in the small cohort of marketing leaders publicly shaping the governance and brand questions that agentic AI raises, specifically, how leadership principles should be embedded directly into AI architecture rather than applied after the fact.
profiles.name: Christy Borrowman

profiles.hook: Cosoreanu spent nearly two decades rising through GE's energy technology divisions, engineering, program management, and eventually product and CTO roles in grid automation, before taking the CTO seat at GE Vernova as the company builds the grid infrastructure and automation technology the energy transition depends on.
profiles.name: Claudia Cosoreanu
profiles.moniker: Chief Technology Officer at GE Vernova

primary.name: Claudia Cosoreanu, MBA, PEng, LinkedIn profile

profiles.hook: Bell moved from theoretical chemistry research at Berkeley and Caltech into technology leadership at Uber, then led data science and AI organizations across four different industries, energy at bp, automotive at Ford, and now retail at The Home Depot, one of the few executives to have run enterprise AI at that scale in more than one sector.
profiles.name: Franziska Bell
profiles.moniker: CTO of The Home Depot, Four-Industry Technology Executive

profiles.hook: Mineart began as a mechanical engineer at Caterpillar in 1999 and spent nearly three decades rising through engineering, product strategy, and electric power leadership roles before being named Chief Technology Officer, now leading Cat Technology's push to integrate smarter, more connected machines across Caterpillar's global equipment lines.
profiles.name: Jaime Mineart

profiles.hook: Fowler ran technology for one of America's largest industrial conglomerates, GE, where he oversaw a $3 billion budget and 25,000 employees and drove the insourcing of thousands of technology jobs, before leading Nationwide's digital transformation and now shaping Lumen's AI-driven network strategy as its CTPO.
profiles.name: Jim Fowler
profiles.moniker: Chief Technology and Product Officer at Lumen Technologies

profiles.hook: Milchanowski built her career at the intersection of AI and financial crime, from model risk management at JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley to leading a global AI and quantum lab at EY that supported the U.S. National Security Commission on Artificial Intelligence, before becoming BMO's first Chief AI and Quantum Officer and founding director of its applied AI institute.
profiles.name: Kristin Milchanowski
profiles.moniker: Chief AI and Quantum Officer at BMO Financial Group

profiles.hook: Beck has spent over 17 years inside Daimler's IT organisation, running IT for Daimler Trucks Asia and Mitsubishi Fuso from Tokyo before becoming CIO of Daimler Truck North America in 2018, where he also now heads IT for autonomous driving. He speaks German, English, French, and Spanish.
profiles.name: Lutz Beck

profiles.hook: Mehrotra built Allstate's entire AI Center of Excellence from the ground up, an 80-plus person team and a multi-year generative AI strategy, and now applies that same enterprise-AI playbook as Chief AI Officer at U.S. Bank.
profiles.name: Prashant Mehrotra
profiles.moniker: Chief AI Officer at U.S. Bank

profiles.hook: Naga's entire executive career was built inside two companies that run some of the largest real-time systems on Earth, LinkedIn and Uber, rising internally at Uber over eleven years to become CTO of a platform operating across cities, countries, and hundreds of millions of users.
profiles.name: Praveen Neppalli Naga

profiles.hook: Ummadisetti has been building production generative AI systems, RAG pipelines, model fine-tuning, agentic platforms, since before the term agentic AI entered general use. At Toyota North America he leads the function responsible for autonomous AI agents in one of the world's largest automotive manufacturers, while his seat on the LangChain advisory board gives him direct influence on the open-source tooling that most agentic systems are built on.
profiles.name: Ravi Chandu Ummadisetti
profiles.moniker: Head of Agentic AI at Toyota North America

profiles.hook: Katti built his career on the unglamorous but essential problem of moving data efficiently, first in academic networking research, then running Intel's networking hardware division, and now at OpenAI, where the physical compute infrastructure behind frontier AI models is his direct responsibility.
profiles.name: Sachin Katti
profiles.moniker: OpenAI's Head of Compute and Former Stanford Networking Professor

primary.name: Sachin Katti, Stanford EE faculty profile (archival)

secondary.name: Intel names Sachin Katti CTO of Network and Edge Group, Intel Newsroom (2020)

profiles.hook: Nandy spent over 15 years building the infrastructure behind Google's core advertising and analytics businesses, systems used by billions of people, before leading product and engineering at Okta's identity platform and now steering Docusign's shift toward AI-driven agreement management as CTO.
profiles.name: Sagnik Nandy
profiles.moniker: Chief Technology Officer at Docusign, Former Google VP

profiles.hook: Venkatesan has spent 25 years running the technology behind some of the largest consumer platforms in commerce and advertising, eBay, StubHub, Marketo, Yahoo, Walmart, and now PayPal, where he leads AI and machine learning across the company's entire payments ecosystem.
profiles.name: Srini Venkatesan
profiles.moniker: EVP and Chief Technology Officer at PayPal

profiles.hook: Kirkeberg spent over a decade building the cloud infrastructure underneath Norway's sovereign wealth fund before pivoting to build its AI function from nothing, growing it into a 71-member AI Ambassador network across Oslo, London, New York, and Singapore with measured efficiency gains rather than speculative claims.
profiles.name: Stian Kirkeberg
profiles.moniker: Head of AI & ML at Norway's Sovereign Wealth Fund

primary.name: Norges Bank Investment Management, official site

profiles.hook: Ambrozie has led digital transformation at three of the largest consumer-facing organizations in America, Ford, Disney Parks, and now CVS Health, bringing consumer-experience engineering discipline to bear on making AI-driven healthcare personalization work at national scale.
profiles.name: Tony Ambrozie
profiles.moniker: Healthcare's Digital and AI Transformation Executive

primary.name: Tony Ambrozie, official executive bio, CVS Health Newsroom

profiles.hook: Childers moved from Fortune 20 operations, Amazon's peak IT infrastructure and GE's global virtualization program, into the CIO seat at a precision aerospace manufacturer. His IoT initiative at Meyer Tool, measuring machine productivity and availability on the factory floor, is the kind of applied industrial AI that rarely makes headlines but represents the actual frontier of operational technology in advanced manufacturing.
profiles.name: Vern Childers
